analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read is caused by calling ReplaceTextureWithColor() on textures whose pixel buffer can be smaller than one aiTexel. ParseTextureColorData() allocates pcData as new aiTexel[mWidth*mHeight] with unchecked dimensions; with crafted MDL7/HMP skin metadata this can produce a tiny allocation (seen as 1 byte in ASan due to overflow/size confusion in element count), but ParseSkinLump_3DGS_MDL7 still unconditionally invokes ReplaceTextureWithColor(). ReplaceTextureWithColor() then iterates aiTexel elements and dereferences *(pcTexel-1)/ *pcTexel, causing read past the allocated heap region (crash in aiTexel::operator!= at texture.h:102).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: From assimp_fuzzer input, HMP7 parsing reaches HMPImporter::ReadFirstSkin(), which forwards attacker-controlled skin type/width/height to MDLImporter::ParseSkinLump_3DGS_MDL7(). The path must create an embedded color texture branch (not external-file/referrer/DDS-only), so ParseTextureColorData() is called with those dimensions. If width*height is malformed (e.g., overflow/invalid tiny effective allocation) and no validation rejects it, pcNew is still passed to ReplaceTextureWithColor(), which assumes at least valid aiTexel array bounds and performs linear aiTexel comparisons, triggering heap-buffer-overflow read.
